Forme juridique de l'attributaire Le marché public sera conclu : – soit avec un opérateur économique unique ; 8/17 – soit avec un groupement d’opérateurs économiques conjoint ou solidaire. En cas de groupement conjoint, le mandataire sera solidaire, pour l'exécution du marché public, de chacun des membres du groupement, pour ses obligations contractuelles à l'égard de l’acheteur. La composition du groupement ne peut être modifiée entre la remise des offres et la date de signature du contrat. 2-6. ant indiquant qu'il ne tombe pas sous le coup d'une interdiction de soumissionner. Pour satisfaire aux obligations susmentionnées, le candidat qui envisage, dès le dépôt de son offre, de sous-traiter une partie de sa prestation, complètera utilement la déclaration de sous - traitance et joindra, pour chaque sous-traitant, l’ensemble des documents, attestations et renseignements réclamés aux candidats, tels que figurant au présent règlement de la consultation. La notification du marché public emporte acceptation du sous-traitant et agrément des conditions de paiement. Les prestations de services sont prouvées par des attestations du destinataire ou, à défaut, par une déclaration de l'opérateur économique ; • Une déclaration indiquant les effectifs moyens annuels du candidat et l'importance du personnel d'encadrement pendant les trois dernières années ; • Une description de l'outillage, du matériel et de l'équipement technique dont le candidat disposera pour la réalisation du marché public.  REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

UGANDA DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT – GOVERNMENT NETWORK (UDAP-GOVNET)

PROJECT ID: P171305

LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980

 

REFERENCE NUMBER: NITA-UDAP/CONS/26-27/00027

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS TRAINING PROGRAMME (NDSTP)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority – Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project – Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy services for the implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP)

 

The con

responsibility of implementation of the National Digital Skills Training Programme (NDSTP) programme across Uganda. The assignment will equip at least 6,000 beneficiaries drawn from public servants, teachers and tutors, out-of-school youth, refugees and refugee-host communities, and persons with disabilities with the digital knowledge and practical competencies needed to access services safely and productively, pursue education and livelihood opportunities, and participate as informed digital citizens.

The duration of the assignment will be five (5) months from the date of contract signing.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be accessed at https://www.nita.go.ug

The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the services. insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

Rationale 1.1 Compliance with Terms of Reference’s Requirements - Mandatory The Economic Operator shall submit a narrative of approximately 1,000 words demonstrating a clear and comprehensive understanding of the national GBV/DV campaign context (ref. Terms of Reference Article 2.1 – Overall Objectives). The narrative must explain how the Contracting Authority’s briefs will be interpreted and translated into coherent campaign concepts, with specific reference to Terms of Reference Article 1.1 and 4.2.1 (Campaign Strategy and Pre Launch). (i) Methodology for interpreting briefs and translating them into strategic campaign themes. (5 marks) (ii) End-to-end progression from strategy insight and executional outputs (4 marks) (iii

d on the basis of the following: • Accuracy and depth of understanding of the GBV/DV strategic framework • Ability to translate Terms of Reference requirements into a structured, campaign approach • Quality and logic of the proposed rationale • Structured methodology from briefs → themes → execution • Clear alignment with the National Strategy]]></label> <threshold>1</threshold> <value/> </criterion> <criterion level="2" pos="2" id="17877278647823" mandatory="1" included-in-evaluation="1" weight="12" type="file"> <weighted-score/> <label><![CDATA[1.2 Risks and Assumptions - Mandatory The Economic Operator shall submit a detailed Risk and Mitigation Report of approximately 1,000 words outlining key risks and mitigation measures relating to planning and approvals, resource and deadline management, flexibility, quality assurance, language clarity, and confidentiality/data protection, in accordance with Terms of Reference Articles 4.1–4.3. (i) Identification and clarity of risks and potential impacts (4 marks) (ii) Practicality, quality, robustness, and feasibility of mitigation measures (4 marks) (iii) Relevance and linkage of risks to Terms of Reference deliverables and timelines (2 marks) (iv) Awareness of operational constrain
